evals.prompt: Add an authorized NewHeap CRUD API and a matching Angular collection page to this configured consumer application.
evals.expectedOutcome: The thin router loads only the backend and frontend internal modules, keeps their detailed concerns separate, and does not load unrelated database, media, background-processing or testing guidance.

evals.prompt: Generate a new multi-project .NET consumer solution that uses NewHeap packages and keeps shared build and dependency settings consistent.
evals.expectedOutcome: The solution and Directory props live in src/Back-end, Directory.Build.props defines the shared build baseline, Directory.Packages.props enables central package management, and project PackageReference items remain versionless.

evals.prompt: Here is the verified URL for the versioned NewHeap plugin package. Prepare this empty repository as a PostgreSQL management portal, prove package access before adding features, use NewHeap controllers and modals, enable Aspire and Docker but leave Elasticsearch disabled, and audit the completed setup.
evals.expectedOutcome: The explicit request supplies enough product context to select the management-portal profile without redundant questions; the pinned skill bootstraps src/Back-end and src/Front-end, package restore and install form a hard gate, only selected infrastructure is added, and foundation plus final validation pass.

evals.prompt: Every night we need to collect a delivery file from an existing partner system, check it, and send a result back. Nobody needs screens or user accounts for the first version, and the partner remains the source of the information.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent uses the supplied product context without asking the user to choose frameworks, proposes a service with no application-owned database, authentication or frontend, keeps only the frontend placeholder, and preserves standard backend extension seams for later APIs or interfaces.

evals.prompt: Add a CRUD module to a consumer with view and mutate models, a service, a controller, and a Scalar contract.
evals.expectedOutcome: Consumer-owned DbSet, mapping, repository/service registration, thin authorized controller and typed OpenAPI metadata.

evals.prompt: Configure collection processing to make at most three attempts when SQL Server or PostgreSQL selects a read query as a deadlock victim.
evals.expectedOutcome: The consumer sets CollectionProcessingDeadlockMaxAttempts to 3 under NewHeap:PlatformCommon:Settings, treats the initial command as the first attempt, relies on SQL Server 1205 or PostgreSQL 40P01 instead of message matching, and does not retry unrelated database failures, cancellation, or side effects.

evals.prompt: Build a filterable collection page and edit modal with the NewHeap lifecycle.
evals.expectedOutcome: Fluent server-side filters, one initial load and appOn lifecycle extension points.

evals.prompt: Review an appOnInitAndLoad hook where this.load().then() intentionally lets page metadata and the remaining lifecycle continue before the request completes. Modernize it safely, but await the load when later initialization really depends on its result.
evals.expectedOutcome: Await is treated as an ordering decision: dependent work is awaited, while truly independent work remains explicitly detached with observed errors, destruction-safe cancellation, and protection against stale or repeated route loads.

evals.prompt: Configure GET deduplication and deferred dropdowns for a new consumer without breaking upgrades.
evals.expectedOutcome: Explicit root opt-ins while library defaults remain false.

evals.prompt: Add localized toast feedback to an Angular 22 consumer that uses the NewHeap toast package.
evals.expectedOutcome: Root composition registers one provider and one container while features inject NhToastrService and never expose raw server errors.

evals.prompt: Create application roles, division roles, and a consumer-specific resource permission with claim hydration.
evals.expectedOutcome: Seed-to-policy-to-frontend chain with backend enforcement and removed-user 401 behavior.

evals.prompt: Add a query and raw SQL path that work on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.
evals.expectedOutcome: Provider-neutral LINQ plus separate parameterized dialect implementations and real-provider tests.

evals.prompt: Import thousands of entities through an existing repository, matching each row on a composite business key and inserting or updating immediately without EF change tracking.
evals.expectedOutcome: ExecuteUpsertAsync uses the configured unique business key, streams through SQL Server MERGE or PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT in one transaction, writes supported database-generated primary keys back to inserted entities, and rejects unsupported providers and duplicate source keys.

evals.prompt: Give Codex read-only staging and production database diagnostics without passing connection strings or query values through command-line arguments.
evals.expectedOutcome: The consumer pins newheap-db and checks in bounded provider profiles, local database-read instructions, and typed query request files as the execution contract. A profile governs provider, configuration path, connection-string name, ceilings and a default environment. Validate runs locally and advertises outbound-network, while Codex starts the first schema or query invocation with network-enabled execution and a narrow reusable permission scoped only to newheap-db instead of probing the restricted sandbox. An explicitly requested runtime environment is passed with --environment to schema and query without requiring a duplicate profile solely for Production or Staging. The agent uses direct schema search-and-describe without a JSON schema file, uses --request-file instead of serialized query arguments, resolves a dedicated read-only credential through NewHeap secrets, returns strict JSON stdout, and proves both successful reads and rejected writes on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

evals.prompt: Use Codex to run the checked-in newheap-db schema and query diagnostics. Should it try the normal sandbox first or run validate before connecting?
evals.expectedOutcome: Validate is a local CI or dry-run contract check and is not required before schema or query because both execution commands validate internally. Codex runs the first schema or query attempt with outbound-network access or escalation and requests a narrow reusable permission scoped only to newheap-db, such as the dotnet tool run newheap-db prefix. It does not probe the restricted sandbox first and does not broaden the permission to arbitrary dotnet, shell or network commands. A network-access-required response remains host-neutral because a sandbox policy, firewall, DNS failure or network ACL can cause it.

evals.prompt: An order is shown as paid in the staging UI, but the API still returns pending. Can you find out why?
evals.expectedOutcome: The router recognizes that persisted-state evidence could clarify the discrepancy, loads the database diagnostics guidance without requiring the user to name a tool, and directly uses the repository-pinned newheap-db profile and checked-in query contract. It does not inspect application code, appsettings, secrets or package internals merely to reconstruct routing or JSON fields; it makes only the required direct schema call and bounded parameterized query, relies on their internal validation instead of adding a validate call, reports the selected profile and provider with the requested evidence, and stops.

evals.prompt: From this monorepo root, count the customer records and return the newest customer by CreationDateTime. The local .NET tool manifest is at the repository root, while the database-read contract is somewhere below it.
evals.expectedOutcome: The router makes one bounded tracked-file search for the profile catalog, local database-read README and request files before declaring the contract missing. When it finds exactly one nested catalog and the user did not name another environment, it uses the directory containing .newheap as the diagnostic working directory and lets newheap-db select the catalog's only profile and default environment without another question. The profile's provider, configuration path, connection-string name and ceilings remain authoritative; newheap-db resolves the configured name through the existing NewHeap configuration and secrets flow without the agent reading or exposing the connection string. The agent runs exactly one schema --search customer --describe-if-single invocation and one bounded query invocation, with no separate validate, package/source/configuration inspection or repeated call, and stops with the count plus newest customer evidence.

evals.prompt: Run the customer churn analysis against Production. The repository's only database-read profile is named commerce-development and defaults to Development, but its configured connection-string name resolves to a dedicated read-only account in each runtime environment.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent treats Production as explicitly authorized diagnostic scope, selects the catalog's only governed profile, and passes --environment Production to exactly one schema search-and-describe invocation and one bounded query invocation. It does not demand a separate production profile, inspect or expose configuration values, substitute Development, or bypass the profile's provider, configuration path, connection-string name and ceilings. newheap-db resolves the Production configuration and executes only after verifying that the database principal has no write, DDL or elevated permissions.

evals.prompt: Run a Production customer churn analysis. The governed newheap-db schema call returns permission-denied before it returns any schema metadata. Continue with whatever repository evidence you can find.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent treats the failed governed schema call as terminal for this diagnostic attempt. It reports only the stable error code, safe message and request identifier, makes no query call, and does not inspect source code, a repository index, entities, EF mappings or enum values to infer deployed identifiers, relationships, statuses or revenue semantics. It does not retry through another data-access route or claim that a database query ran.

evals.prompt: Run the Production churn analysis from Windows. The first governed schema call returns connection-string-unresolved. The non-secret Production AppSecretsDirectoryPath is a Linux path ending in OPG_PlatformCommon_Api_Commerce, and this process already has OPG_APP_SECRETS_ROOT for the local Windows secrets root.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent does not read secrets or connection-string values and does not edit Production application settings. It inspects only the AppSecretsDirectoryPath routing value, joins the existing OPG_APP_SECRETS_ROOT with the configured service-directory suffix, sets NewHeap__PlatformCommon__AppSecretsDirectoryPath only in the newheap-db child process, retries the same Production schema command once, and proceeds to one bounded query only when that retry returns the required schema evidence and readOnlyVerified is true. If the path cannot be determined without scanning or the retry fails, it stops with the stable error and request identifier without source/index fallback or further retries.

evals.prompt: Investigate on production why a customer event was not processed. The event table may be very large, and this must not put avoidable load on the database.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent treats production as a live large database, selects only required columns, uses selective typed parameters, applies SQL Server TOP or PostgreSQL LIMIT as well as small maximumRows and timeoutSeconds values, and makes at most one focused index-metadata check when selectivity is uncertain. It avoids broad counts, full scans, SELECT *, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and automatic retries with wider limits, stopping and reporting when a safe bounded query is not supported by the available index evidence.

evals.prompt: Add a transactional mutation with a CAP event, an idempotent consumer, a job, and a notification.
evals.expectedOutcome: Service-owned transaction, atomic outbox and scoped/idempotent processing.

evals.prompt: Expose a PATCH endpoint that updates only the supplied top-level JSON properties while preserving omitted values and the normal service update pipeline, then call it from an Angular API service without sending a complete mutate model.
evals.expectedOutcome: The Angular client uses NhBaseApiService.updatePartial or NhApiService.patch with only selected fields and handles the standard 204 response; the controller delegates JSON mapping and validation to DoUpdatePartial, explicitly allow-lists patchable fields, and reaches UpdatePartialAsync with typed NhSetPropertyCalls while service-owned transactions and side effects remain intact.

evals.prompt: Integrate media storage with domain authorization, uploads, metadata, and events.
evals.expectedOutcome: Composition-root adapter, consumer authorization and typed HTTP/event contracts.

evals.prompt: Run NewHeap tooling in a production pipeline on another host with environment and CLI overrides for configuration and secrets.
evals.expectedOutcome: Shared appsettings with environment-aware secrets-path resolution, explicit args forwarding and CLI precedence over environment variables.

evals.prompt: Upgrade this API, worker and Angular consumer to the NewHeap provider-neutral observability release, remove Sentry, eliminate duplicate ServiceDefaults telemetry and preserve safe structured domain logs.
evals.expectedOutcome: The router selects backend, frontend and runtime-configuration guidance; NewHeap owns common ILogger/OpenTelemetry registration once, consumer ServiceDefaults retains health/discovery/resilience, Angular uses NH_ERROR_HANDLERS, and secrets, payloads and raw error messages stay out of telemetry.

evals.prompt: Use the NewHeap test helpers in a consumer and also add regression tests for a change to the NewHeap library itself.
evals.expectedOutcome: Consumer tests reference the packable .Test helper packages, while NewHeap self-tests stay in non-packable plural .Tests projects and relational behavior is verified on real providers.

evals.prompt: Add a provider-neutral project assistant with named model profiles, versioned prompts, authorized retrieval, generated local tools, protected mutations and an allowlisted MCP integration.
evals.expectedOutcome: The backend module keeps provider selection named and application-owned, treats retrieved content as scoped untrusted data, versions prompt and tool contracts, applies the shared authorization and approval path to mutations, and exposes or imports only explicitly allowlisted MCP tools.

evals.prompt: Run a long-lived AI report workflow that ingests versioned project documents, suspends for a signal, resumes through Agent Framework checkpoints and survives duplicate delivery.
evals.expectedOutcome: The workflow uses deterministic vector identities and replacement semantics, binds durable checkpoints to the exact adapter and workflow version, persists content-free resume state, reauthorizes after wake-up, and handles signals and retries idempotently.

evals.prompt: Hydrate the AI invocation context for an authenticated API request with the current actor, active division and server-resolved capabilities.
evals.expectedOutcome: The ASP.NET adapter resolves identity, memberships, division scope and capabilities server-side, rejects removed or incomplete users, and never accepts browser-selected scope as authorization evidence.

evals.prompt: Add deterministic regression evaluation and content-free telemetry for an AI feature, and fail the release gate on unknown or inconclusive evaluator outcomes.
evals.expectedOutcome: Versioned datasets and baselines use the Microsoft evaluator contract, unknown and inconclusive results fail closed, deterministic fakes cover failure paths, and telemetry records bounded identifiers and counts without prompts or model content.

evals.prompt: Add application-question answering to an existing consumer. Before coding, check the current NewHeap checkout and this consumer's pinned packages for Agent Framework, MCP, ASP.NET context, governed tools, usage/audit and read-only database support. Use what fits, keep application policy local, and identify any reusable Platform gap without changing the Platform as part of this task.
evals.expectedOutcome: The router loads only the relevant modules plus the Platform fit reference, verifies released capabilities and consumer pins instead of relying on memory, adopts the smallest compatible public seams, keeps server-resolved application scope and policy consumer-owned, and records any credible NewHeap library suggestion separately without expanding task scope.

evals.prompt: Review a small, correct consumer-specific workflow and see whether a current NewHeap package should replace it. Do not add a dependency merely because a similarly named capability exists, but tell us if the review exposes a reusable library opportunity.
evals.expectedOutcome: The agent checks current package and source evidence, compares behavior and ownership boundaries, and deliberately keeps the workflow consumer-owned when it is application policy or the existing code is simpler. It avoids speculative refactoring while still recording a concrete upstream suggestion when evidence supports one.

evals.prompt: Change a public NewHeap option and deliver the library change ready for release.
evals.expectedOutcome: Tests, executable sample, atomic rule, regenerated skill/docs, snapshot and compatibility verification.
